title: Verifier‑Grounded Paired Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations (Preregistered estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; shared_initial_candidate)
abstract: We present a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that compares a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks using a deterministic validator. The preregistered estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (i.e., a single canonical LLM candidate per pair reused for both scoring conditions). Under these frozen semantics the run completed with baseline = 120/120 verifier passes and guarded = 120/120 verifier passes; paired difference = 0.00 (95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00]; bootstrap seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We (1) publish the exact execution and analysis artifacts and SHA‑256 fingerprints required to reproduce every step, (2) use the archived traces to diagnose why the preregistered shared_initial_candidate design produced a degenerate paired contingency, and (3) provide artifact‑grounded runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed replication, validator diversification, and broader task heterogeneity) that preserve reproducibility while answering the operational question of independent generative reliability. Representative artifact fingerprints: execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820; execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...; execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f....

sections.introduction: Translating high‑level operator intent into device configurations is a core NetOps workflow where semantic correctness (reachability, ACL/routing invariants, and safe transient states) is safety‑critical. Deterministic offline validators (reachability/ACL/routing analyzers) are widely used operationally to check candidate configurations before deployment [10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Large language models (LLMs) can propose fluent intent→config candidates rapidly, but evaluating their operational reliability requires verifier‑grounded metrics and careful experimental semantics. We preregistered CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1 to test a narrow, clearly specified estimand: the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (a single canonical candidate generated per task and reused for both scoring conditions). This paper (i) publishes complete execution and analysis artifacts for byte‑for‑byte reproduction, (ii) reports the preregistered confirmatory outcome, and (iii) uses the archived traces to diagnose why the chosen confirmatory semantics produced a degenerate but internally valid contingency table and to propose deterministic, runnable reruns that answer the operational independence question.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded evaluation and generate–validate–repair architectures are established patterns in NetOps research and practice. Batfish and its successors provide high‑fidelity offline analyses of forwarding, reachability, and ACL semantics and have been used to validate configuration correctness at scale [10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Recent LLM→NetOps studies vary methodologically on (A) sampling semantics (single canonical candidate vs independent per‑condition sampling), (B) repair budgets (single pass vs bounded iterative repair), and (C) validator scope (syntactic parsing only vs full transient and final‑state checks). Studies that adopt independent per‑condition sampling and multi‑seed replication directly estimate the deployment‑relevant probability that independently drawn LLM outputs satisfy verifier constraints; studies that reuse a single canonical candidate per pair test a different estimand—validator consistency given identical inputs. Our contribution is an exhaustive, artifact‑anchored execution that makes those distinctions explicit and reproducible.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design. The preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; SHA‑256 7db1663cf398...) fixed: N = 120 paired tasks (40 per topology class), primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, confirmatory generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, single canonical seed_0 per task for paired analysis, deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5, and the exact inference rules (paired_binary_analysis_v1 with bootstrap parameters: 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Task synthesis. Tasks were programmatically generated from deterministic templates (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) encoding initial_state, expected_final_state, explicit required_sequence, and per‑task workflow_policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups). Tasks intentionally include operational transient constraints (make‑before‑break, atomic MTU changes) so the validator checks have operational meaning. Model and orchestration. The declared LLM was gpt‑5‑mini accessed via hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (see execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2...). Under the shared_initial_candidate protocol, one canonical generation per task was produced and then reused for both scoring episodes; those canonical candidate files are archived (e.g., execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8be...). Validator and scoring. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (version 5.0) parses and normalizes commands, enforces per‑task workflow_policies (transient safety checks), and asserts final_state invariants. The scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation yields a binary pass only when all required commands and transient constraints are satisfied. All per‑episode validator traces are archived under execution/scoring/*.json (representative: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...). Execution accounting and reproducibility. Planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; model_calls_used = 120 (one canonical generation per task); failed_episode_count = 0. The complete execution and artifact manifest (with per‑file SHA‑256 fingerprints) is included in the bundle (execution/execution_manifest.json).
sections.results: Confirmatory outcome (artifact‑anchored). All preregistered confirmatory episodes completed and are archived. Observed counts: N = 120 paired tasks; baseline_success_count = 120/120; guarded_success_count = 120/120. Paired contingency: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...). Primary estimator (mean of guarded_i − baseline_i) = 0.00. A 10,000‑resample percentile bootstrap (seed = 1729) yields 95% CI [0.00, 0.00]. Exact McNemar two‑sided test: p = 1.0. Representative per‑episode traces illustrate validator behavior: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...) records parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, and validation_after.valid = true; the canonical candidate used is execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...). Why the confirmatory contrast is degenerate. The archived causal chain shows two preregistered, artifact‑visible design choices produced deterministically identical scored inputs per pair: (1) confirmatory generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one canonical LLM candidate generated per task and reused verbatim for both baseline and guarded scoring episodes; see execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt), and (2) template‑tight task synthesis that encoded explicit required_sequences/workflow_policies satisfied by template‑aligned candidates. Because the validator is deterministic, identical inputs necessarily produce identical pass/fail outputs, collapsing the paired contingency to n_11 = 120. The execution manifest, response files, and per‑episode scoring traces precisely document this chain and permit byte‑for‑byte replication.
sections.discussion: What the confirmatory result legitimately shows. The confirmatory statistics correctly answer the preregistered estimand: whether a deterministic validator gives different pass/fail outcomes when presented with identical canonical candidates across two scoring conditions; the answer is no (paired difference = 0). What it does not show. It does not estimate the operational quantity NetOps practitioners commonly require—the independent probability that independently sampled LLM outputs satisfy verifier constraints—because the confirmatory design deliberately removed inter‑condition generation variance via shared_initial_candidate. Runnable, artifact‑grounded modifications. Using only the archived artifacts and orchestration code one can deterministically rerun informative variants without inventing new data: (A) independent_per_condition rerun: draw an independent seed per condition per task (baseline_seed != guarded_seed), regenerate candidates, rescore with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and compute paired contrasts; (B) multi‑seed confirmatory design: draw K ≥ 3 independent seeds per condition per task and estimate per‑condition pass probabilities with bootstrap CIs; (C) validator diversification: add an independent verifier and report intersection/union pass rates. All inputs, seeds, provider calls, and validator traces required to replay or extend the experiment are archived (see execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/call_cache/). Threats to validity (artifact‑identified). Internal validity: shared_initial semantics removed generation variance by design. Construct validity: template‑aligned tasks and a single deterministic validator can overestimate success for open‑distribution intents. External validity: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic tasks limit generalization. Contamination: preregistered string‑overlap heuristics flagged no confirmatory contamination under chosen thresholds, but heuristics are imperfect proxies for pretraining exposure. All of these limitations are visible and traceable in the published artifacts.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired experiment and released exhaustive artifacts enabling byte‑for‑byte reproduction. Under the frozen shared_initial_candidate confirmatory semantics, both the deterministic template baseline and the gpt‑5‑mini guarded condition passed the deterministic validator on all N = 120 tasks (both 120/120), producing a degenerate paired contingency (n_11 = 120). The artifact traces make the causal mechanism explicit: identical canonical candidates reused across conditions plus template‑tight tasks produced identical deterministic validator outcomes. We provide artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed replication, validator diversification) that preserve reproducibility while answering the operational question of independent LLM generative reliability. All execution and analysis artifacts—plus the immutable initial master prompt reference (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and the preregistration SHA‑256—are included in the submission bundle to permit exact audit and deterministic follow‑up reruns.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
